subject: How to upgrade bioconductor version within a packrat controlled project

messages.author: 61221ab1f726dce8
messages.subject: How to upgrade bioconductor version within a packrat controlled project
parts:
Hi,

Is there a correct procedure on upgrading the version of bioconductor in a packrat controlled project? For example, my R-3.1.0 installation is set to use Bioconductor version 2.14:

> library(BiocInstaller)
Bioconductor version 2.14 (BiocInstaller 1.14.2), ?biocLite for help

When I initialize the project to use packrat:

> packrat::init()
Initializing packrat project in directory:
- "/Users/fcchan/test"
--- Please select a CRAN mirror for use in this session ---


Adding these packages to packrat:
            _
    packrat   0.4.1-1



It sets up the packrat/packrat.snapshot as such:

PackratFormat: 1.4
PackratVersion: 0.4.1.1
RVersion: 3.1.0
Repos: CRAN=http://cran.stat.sfu.ca,
    BioCsoft=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/bioc,
    BioCann=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/data/annotation,
    BioCexp=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/data/experiment,
    BioCextra=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/extra


Package: packrat
Source: CRAN
Version: 0.4.1-1
Hash: 5716097644904b9c1b4be2692de1600

This is all fine, but somewhere along the line I realized I need a particular version of a bioconductor package that was only available in Bioconductor 3.0. The R version 3.1.0 has the ability to support both the bioconductor version 2.14 and 3.0. As per the bioconductor manual, one can update the bioconductor like this:

source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
biocLite("BiocUpgrade") ## R version 2.15 or later

Bioconductor version 3.0 (BiocInstaller 1.16.0), ?biocLite for help


Packrat doesn't recognize a Bioconductor package upgrade:

>less packrat/packrat.lock

PackratFormat: 1.4
PackratVersion: 0.4.1.1
RVersion: 3.1.0
Repos: CRAN=http://cran.stat.sfu.ca,
    BioCsoft=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/bioc,
    BioCann=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/data/annotation,
    BioCexp=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/data/experiment,
    BioCextra=http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.14/extra


Package: BiocInstaller
Source: Bioconductor
Version: 1.16.0
Hash: a3c695ccdcf74d999deb8ddc86f8b7e8


Package: packrat
Source: CRAN
Version: 0.4.1-1
Hash: 5716097644904b9c1b4be2692de16005


In fact, the packrat snapshot mechanism fails since it still seeks the bioconductor packages found in the 2.14 repository. I tried to basically manually change the repositories to 3.0, but that came up some weird errors. Is there a proper way to do this?

Thanks,

messages.author: ab0d2be2ea8dabe8
messages.subject: Re: How to upgrade bioconductor version within a packrat controlled project
parts:
When snapshotting a project, packrat looks for the ‘active repositories’ — this is the union of whatever is in getOption('repos'), and the output for BiocInstaller::biocinstallRepos(). Can you confirm a couple things:

  1. What is the output of BiocInstaller::biocinstallRepos()?
  2. What is the output of getOption('repos')?

Performing:

source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
biocLite("BiocUpgrade")

packrat::snapshot()

should be sufficient for updating the packrat project. Can you post the exact errors you’re receiving on packrat::snapshot()?

​

parts:
Okay, I've reproduced this now and it looks like it's a bug in Packrat -- we're not respecting new repositories set as part of BiocInstaller. I'll generate a fix for this and commit to GitHub soon.

As a workaround, you can manually set the repositories:

    options(repos = c(getOption('repos')["CRAN"], BiocInstaller:::biocinstallRepos()))

That should help you resolve the problem in the meantime.
